# Synthetic OneNote Import Corpus

These `.one` files are generated by NoteCraft from synthetic text and asset bytes.
They contain no personal notebooks or copied third-party samples.

Regenerate the files from the repository root:

```text
cargo run -p notecraft-import --example generate_synthetic_fixtures
```

The generator is deterministic. `cargo test -p notecraft-import --test synthetic_corpus`
checks that its output matches the checked-in files and exercises the real importer
in HTML and CMGFM formats.

| File | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `rich-content.one` | Multiple pages, a nested page, bold text, and Arabic text. |
| `page-hierarchy.one` | Three page levels followed by a new top-level page. |
| `formatted-text.one` | Plain, bold, and italic synthetic text runs. |
| `asset-pack.one` | PNG, SVG, attached text file, and a picture with missing data. |
| `versions (On 1-2-2026).one` | Newest copy of one synthetic section. |
| `versions (On 1-2-2025).one` | Older copy; excluded by default version selection. |
| `broken.one` | Truncated section beside valid sections; must be reported without stopping the import. |

This first corpus slice covers `.one` sections supported by the current importer.
It does not establish `.onetoc2`, `.onepkg`, notebook color, ink, table, or full
OneNote parser interoperability coverage. Those need separate builders or cleared
independent samples and explicit tests.

Third-party samples, when cleared for redistribution, belong in the separate `crates/import/tests/fixtures/3p/<source-name>/` tree with source-specific recognition, provenance, and required license notices. They are not part of this synthetic corpus.
